Thanks for the ping. I pulled the HubSpot activity (link: https://hubspot.com/deals/HS-54821) and our promo ledger. Quick points:
- We issued an initial evaluation grant of 150k tokens on 2027-11-04.
- Two manual extensions (20k each) were processed on 2027-12-18 and 2028-01-14.
- There are four distinct accounts tied to the billing email alex@quantumedge.ai (likely multiple squads).

Usage so far: token burn is concentrated in one account; others have <2k tokens consumed. That pattern often indicates teams requesting separate small grants rather than centralizing consumption.

Recommendation: request short evidence of active pilot work (not just intent) — e.g., notebook/output sample or short session recording — before issuing another top-up. If they provide it, we can approve a single consolidated grant and close the loose subaccounts.

If security sees signals of abuse, we should deny. For now I suggest CS asks for evidence and we pause auto-grants.

-Ben

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

I pulled usage logs and ran an account-linking check — attaching a short summary (quantumedge_usage_summary.csv) and a text extract showing shared recovery emails/domains (account-linking-evidence.txt). Key findings:

- Confirmed four accounts with distinct org ids but highly overlapping owner metadata (same phone numbers, IP ranges during first-week signups).
- Only one account has meaningful activity (model queries concentrated over 3 days). The others show token counts in the low hundreds and no repeated sessions.
- No suspicious inbound payment attempts, but pattern is consistent with teams creating multiple evaluation accounts to request repeated credits over time.

My recommendation is to hold on granting another automated promo. Ask the customer for:
  1) A consolidated list of the teams and planned use-cases.
  2) Evidence of active integration (a short clip or notebook export).
  3) Which single account they want to consolidate billing/usage onto.

If they don't supply evidence within 7 days, we should block further promo grants and flag the deal for manual review by Policy. Happy to draft the customer note.

-Monica

Attachments: quantumedge_usage_summary.csv (summary table), account-linking-evidence.txt (signup metadata extract)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Appreciate the fast triage. Good catch, team — this matches several other promo fragmentation patterns we've seen. Action items:

1) Do not approve any additional credits right now. Monica, please send a short, firm but helpful customer-facing email that: acknowledges their request, requests the three items you listed, and explains we will consolidate grants once we have evidence. I can review the draft before send.

2) Ben, update the HubSpot deal (DEAL-54821-QUANTUMEDGE) with the hold reason and set the next follow-up for 7 days. Add a note that future grants require consolidation.

3) Markus, if you see any escalation from the executive team at QuantumEdge, forward to me immediately — we will not make an exception without documented active usage.

Also copy legal/policy in your outreach if the customer pushes for credits without evidence. If they provide plausible evidence, we can approve a one-time consolidated top-up (capped at 50k) and migrate billing.

I'll set a 30-minute internal sync for tomorrow to review if we get materials.

Thanks — Laura
